new_candidates.body: ### Intro Hi all, was checking out the latest mujoco build on a fork I have, and seems that we are importing `from collections.abc import Buffer` in the `mujoco/rendering/filament/renderer.py` file [here](https://github.com/robotics-folks/mujoco/blob/a14dae261aab5c6e8929a57b70598fa9bb453b36/python/mujoco/rendering/filament/renderer.py#L17), which breaks if not using py312+. I checked with the latest version of mujoco in PyPI as well (3.17.0) and I had the same issue, even though the wheels for py311 for linux are hosted there (only support for py310 was dropped yesterday, right?). I'm still using the studio viewer via this call though (maybe this is deprecated?): ```bash python -m mujoco.experimental.studio.viewer --gfx BACKEND --model MODEL ``` Although for just rendering without a viewer, we still go that path on the imports to `Buffer`, so I guess we still break when only using the mujoco rendering for filament in headless mode, right? ### My setup - mujoco : 3.17.0 - api: python - architecture: x86/64 - os: archlinux ### What's happening? What did you expect? Seems the import `from collections.abc import Buffer` is making it break on python<3.12 and mujoco==3.17.0 ### Steps for reproduction ```bash # Install latest mujoco uv pip install mujoco==3.17.0 # Run the studio viewer python -m mujoco.experimental.studio.viewer --gfx vulkan --model model/humanoid/humanoid.xml ``` ### Minimal model for reproduction Just any model will do, like the `model/humanoid/humanoid.xml` ### Code required for reproduction For checking the viewer: ```bash python -m mujoco.experimental.studio.viewer --gfx BACKEND --model MODEL ``` Outside the viewer seems to have the same issue, just trying to use the filament renderer (same code as in the docs, just adapted a bit): ```python # filename: check_render.py import argparse import mujoco import mujoco.experimental.studio.window from mujoco import mjrf from mujoco.rendering.filament import model_scene from mujoco.rendering.filament import renderer import numpy as np from PIL import Image def render(model: mujoco.MjModel, data: mujoco.MjData, width: int, height: int) -> np.ndarray: # create the rendering context ctx = mjrf.Context(mjrf.ContextConfig()) # create a renderer r = renderer.Renderer(ctx) # add lights and renderables defined in the model to a scene in the renderer ms = model_scene.ModelScene(ctx, model, r.scene("scn")) # create the pixel buffer into which we'll render the image pixels = np.empty((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8) # associate the pixel buffer with a render target r.target("out", pixels) # update the lights and renderables with the current `data` state ms.update(data) # define the camera for the view we want to render vcam = mujoco.MjvCamera() mujoco.mjv_defaultFreeCamera(model, vcam) vcam.type = int(mujoco.mjtCamera.mjCAMERA_FIXED) vcam.fixedcamid = 0 # define a view that connects the scene we want to render to an output target view = renderer.View( scene="scn", target="out", camera=mujoco.mjv_camera2GLCamera(model, data, vcam), ) # render the scene; blocks until the render has completed writing to the render target r.render([view]) # return the pixels return pixels def main() -> int: cli = argparse.ArgumentParser() cli.add_argument("--model", type=str, required=True) args = cli.parse_args() model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(args.model) data = mujoco.MjData(model) pixels = render(model, data, 1024, 768) pil_img = Image.fromarray(pixels) pil_img.save("test_render.png") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main()) ``` Just run it like this: ```bash python check_render.py --model YOUR_MODEL ``` A patch for now would be to use `from typing_extensions import Buffer` instead of `from collections.abc import Buffer` , or maybe just use the first one if py311, and use the second one if py312+ (it's dirty though 😅 , the typing extensions seem to work just fine for now). Here is a screenshot of running the script above (similar to the one in the docs on filament renderer [here](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/python.html#filament-rendering)). Sorry haven't had the time to setup the camera correctly to render the humanoid model, but if not using the patch it just crashes. Left is with python 3.12 without any patches, and right is python 3.11 with the patch to use `from typing_extensions import Buffer` ### Confirmations - [x] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting. - [x] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.
